summary: All failed approaches for fixing the Dify SEO/Homes chatbot. Do NOT retry any of these.

attempts.what: Native Ollama plugin (langgenius/ollama/ollama) pointing to cloud model stubs
attempts.root_cause: SSRF proxy (squid) blocked host.docker.internal. Even after allowlisting, plugin sent malformed auth headers.

attempts.what: Added host.docker.internal to squid allowlist + /etc/hosts mapping
attempts.root_cause: Plugin internals sent auth header even to local Ollama (which needs no auth), causing 401

attempts.what: Switched all 3 apps to openai_api_compatible provider + Ollama Cloud credential
attempts.root_cause: The openai_api_compatible plugin was NEVER INSTALLED via Dify plugin marketplace. Only exists in provider_models table, not in providers table. Dify reads from 'model' JSON column, not 'provider' column.

attempts.what: Switched apps back to langgenius/ollama/ollama via UPDATE provider column only
attempts.error: Provider langgenius/openai/openai does not exist (same error persisted)
attempts.root_cause: Dify reads the 'model' JSON column, NOT the 'provider' column. The model JSON still had "provider":"langgenius/openai/openai"

attempts.what: Fixed model JSON column to langgenius/ollama/ollama with gemma4:31b-cloud
attempts.root_cause: Provider_models table had stale/conflicting entries. Dify validates model name against provider_models before accepting.

attempts.what: Changed model_id and model JSON to gemma4:31b (no -cloud suffix)
attempts.error: Model gemma4:31b credentials is not initialized
attempts.root_cause: Credential existed but wasn't properly linked, OR local Ollama doesn't have gemma4:31b without cloud stub

attempts.what: Deleted and recreated provider_credential + relinked in providers table
attempts.error: Model gemma4:31b-cloud not exist (back to original error)
attempts.root_cause: provider_models DELETE/INSERT didn't take effect (Redis cache? Wrong tenant? Race condition?)
SECRET_KEY mismatch between current .env and when the account was created. Encryption key changed.
Same encryption key mismatch — password is irrelevant, the stored encrypted data can't be decrypted
Flask CLI in Dify container hangs or takes too long

attempts.what: NULL'd password + password_salt in accounts table
attempts.root_cause: NULL password doesn't allow login — need flask create-account to hash properly, but flask CLI hangs

attempts.what: Patched Ollama cloud stub blob JSON files on Windows to add model_format/family/type metadata
attempts.error: Model deepseek-v4-pro:cloud not exist — still fails after blob patching + daemon restart
attempts.root_cause: Plugin daemon only discovers 'ollama' as installed model (log: 'Installed model: ollama'). Cloud stub variants are never registered regardless of blob metadata. Plugin daemon model discovery != provider_models table. The customizable-model provider requires models to be added via UI, and the plugin daemon only lists what the Ollama server reports — but cloud stubs return minimal data.
attempts.lesson: Blob patching changes /api/tags output but plugin daemon doesn't use /api/tags for model discovery — it uses the Ollama Go client library directly which may have different behavior for cloud stubs.

working_state.detail: docker exec dify-worker-1 curl http://host.docker.internal:11434/api/chat with model 'gemma4:31b-cloud' returns valid response. Cloud stubs route to ollama.com transparently.

key_insights: Dify reads model config from app_model_configs.model (JSON column), NOT provider/model_id columns
Admin login is PERMANENTLY BROKEN — SECRET_KEY mismatch. All config changes MUST be via direct SQL
Redis caches model configs — always FLUSHALL after DB changes
provider_models table must have exact model name that appears in ollama /api/tags
The openai_api_compatible plugin was NEVER INSTALLED — don't try using it
Local Ollama with :cloud stubs WORKS from worker container — it's the Dify config layer that's broken
Plugin daemon model discovery is separate from provider_models table. The Ollama plugin only installs 'ollama' model name. Cloud stub variants are NOT automatically discovered.
